title: boot-harness.json — did the scanned repository's application actually start
description: Emitted by bin/boot-harness.sh. Container-only by operator ruling (GATE A, option A): this lane executes the scanned repository's code, so it never runs on the host. The document exists to distinguish four states a reader must never conflate — not attempted, not bootable, bootable but did not boot, and running — because only the last makes the runtime lanes meaningful and the other three are voids rather than passes.

ran.description: false means the harness declined before trying (skipped). NOT a statement about the repo.

skipped.description: Present only when ran is false. Pairs with reason.

bootable.description: Whether the repo ships something this harness knows how to start (compose or Dockerfile). false is a COVERAGE VOID, not a defect in the repo.

booted.description: Whether it actually came up. booted:false with bootable:true is the interesting state — it shipped a stack that did not start here.

needsConfig.description: The stack wants configuration the repository does not ship. Deliberately distinguished from a boot failure: it would boot for its maintainer, and the harness will not invent credentials to make a number look better.

reason.description: Required in every non-booting state — a void with no stated cause is unactionable, and the four causes need four different responses.

project.description: The compose project name, so a leaked stack can be found and torn down by hand.
